1
Concrete has a density of 2400 kg m–3.
Which mass of concrete fills a rectangular space of dimensions 8.0 cm × 90 cm × 110 cm?
A
79 kg
B
190 kg
C
790 kg
D
1900 kg

hints: Notice the mismatch: the three sides are in $\text{cm}$ but density is in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$, so the volume must end up in $\text{m}^3$.
First find the rectangular volume with $V = length \times width \times height$ after changing $8.0 \text{ cm}$, $90 \text{ cm}$ and $110 \text{ cm}$ to metres.
Then use $mass = density \times volume$ with $2400 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and check that the result is near $200 \text{ kg}$.
walkthrough: Convert each length to metres: $8.0 \text{ cm} = 0.080 \text{ m}$, $90 \text{ cm} = 0.90 \text{ m}$ and $110 \text{ cm} = 1.10 \text{ m}$.
Use $m = \rho V$ for mass from density: $m = 2400 \times 0.0792$.
Evaluate: $m = 190.08 \text{ kg}$, which to two significant figures is about $190 \text{ kg}$ with correct unit $\text{kg}$.

A.explanation: This is about 10 times too small and results from a factor-of-10 error in converting $\text{cm}$ to $\text{m}$ or $\text{cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$.

B.explanation: Volume $0.0792 \text{ m}^3$ multiplied by $2400 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ gives about $190 \text{ kg}$.

C.explanation: This is too large and results from using the volume in $\text{cm}^3$ without converting correctly to $\text{m}^3$.

D.explanation: This is about 10 times too large and results from misplacing the decimal point when converting the $8.0 \text{ cm}$ side to metres.
